output.methodChoice: Competing hypotheses (D) plus careful reasoning: the four stories are rival explanations, and a split of rejects by press, supplier and shift discriminates between them.
output.brief: The rejects come from the combination of Arnholt resin and the degraded Press 5 dryer (D5). Arnholt on Press 5 rejects about 10% on both shifts and for new and experienced operators alike. Arnholt on Press 7 rejects 0.8%. Quillan on Press 5 rejects 0.9%. The same Arnholt lot rejected 10.4% through D5 and 0.8% through a good portable dryer. Arnholt arrives wetter (0.27–0.33%), and D5 can't dry it below the 0.20% limit. Second shift looks worse only because all of its VX runs on Press 5. The new operators are not the cause, so don't put them on improvement plans. Dropping Arnholt isn't needed either. Confidence is high, about 90%. One caveat: the Arnholt samples all sat in the north annex, so I can't separate annex storage from the resin itself. That doesn't change this week's action. Repair D5 (heater and desiccant), restore the −40 °C alarm limit and verify the dew point. Until then keep Arnholt off D5, and add a feed-throat moisture check for each resin lot. Look at annex storage later. Moving everything to rented space now would be premature.
